findings.title: GPU path never writes results back to `EntityManager.state`, so spawn/despawn re-upload uses stale data
findings.description:
- On the CPU path, `tick()` mutates `entity_manager.state` in place. On the GPU path, positions and velocities live in GPU fields. The only copy returned is the `TickResult`. Nothing in the design copies it back into `entity_manager.state`.
- `sync_from_entity_manager()` (:89-90, :178-179) re-uploads "CPU state" after a count change. That state is still the startup snapshot, so every surviving agent would teleport back to its initial position on any spawn or despawn.
- Other consumers of `entity_manager.state` would also see frozen data. These include `environment.pre_tick/post_tick`, the spawn and despawn selection logic, and the sim logger.
- The design never says which side owns authoritative state. The plan's "handles spawn/despawn (re-upload changed agent state)" is therefore not deliverable as written.
- `setup_from_server()` sizes the fields from `entity_manager.count` (:144). Quadrants fields are fixed-size, and `finalize()` calls `qd.reset()`. A spawn that raises the count above the allocated capacity has no stated reallocation or capacity strategy.
- `count_changed_since_last_tick()` compares counts only. A despawn plus spawn in the same tick, or a profile or leadership change on an existing agent, would not trigger a re-upload.
- The design needs to:
  - state who owns authoritative state;
  - define the write-back (or a dirty-flag protocol) from `TickResult` to `entity_manager.state`;
  - define the capacity and reallocation policy.

findings.title: Bounds sync-back uploads only positions; reflect and soft modify velocities
findings.description:
- `apply_bounds_policy` is called with both `positions` and `velocities` (:186-191). The sync-back path, `notify_positions_modified` and `upload_positions`, returns only positions to the GPU (:213, :227).
- If reflect or soft change velocities, which is the normal behavior for reflection, those changes are discarded. Agents would then re-hit the boundary each tick.
- Success criterion A4 ("all four policies produce valid positions") would be unmet for these policies.
- Either sync velocities too, or state why `apply_bounds_policy` never alters them.
- Testing covers only wrap (test 7, :315). Add reflect and soft cases.

findings.title: The A7 fallback is not implemented by `_select_arch()` as specified, and it contradicts the default
findings.description:
- `_select_arch()` branches on `platform.system()` only: Darwin returns Metal and Linux returns CUDA. A Linux host with no CUDA driver, such as CI or a headless box, still gets `qd.cuda`, so `qd.init` fails and the server exits.
- The plan entry and A7 promise a fallback "if neither is detected". The design delivers one only for Windows and other platforms.
- Because `quadrants` is the default, this affects every non-GPU Linux host.
- The design needs a real capability check, or a stated `qd.init` failure-to-CPU strategy with a WARNING.
- The doc also never says where `_select_arch()` lives. The scope says it is "updated from the bench backend version", but the bench harness is declared untouched (:40). The mapping from the arch object to the `arch` property string is also unspecified.

findings.title: Verification walkthrough and tests contradict the `quadrants` default
findings.description:
- "CPU default (no GPU)" says that removing the `compute:` block should produce no GPU initialization. That contradicts the stated default of `quadrants` (:33, :61) and test 1 (:309).
- Metal step 1 has the user add `compute:` to `default.yaml` and step 5 says "restore `backend: cpu`". Files Changed says the block is added commented out (:298).
- The testing section says "All tests are CPU-only" (:307) but also lists GPU-required tests.
- Fix these so the acceptance walkthrough matches the design.

findings.title: Open Notes prohibit repeated `qd.init()` in a process, but Testing has no isolation strategy
findings.description:
- The Open Notes call a second `qd.init()` in the same process undefined behavior (:382). Tests 5-8 each call `setup()`, so they would run in one pytest process.
- The isolation requirement lives in a note and is not in the test plan.
- No test covers:
  - the fallback (A7);
  - a `qd.init` or setup failure being logged and exiting at startup;
  - the observable signal for any failure mode.
- A runtime GPU error (kernel fault, OOM mid-session) is declared fatal (:382). The design does not say how that is surfaced from `step()` or what the server tick loop does with it.

findings.title: CPU-path inputs are silently ignored on the GPU path
findings.description:
- The GPU branch ignores `self._forces`, `self._spatial`, and `seasonal_parameter`. The fused kernel hardcodes the seven forces.
- Profiles are frozen at `setup()`.
- If the force configuration (`_build_forces`) or `environment.pre_tick` alters forces or profile parameters, GPU behavior diverges from CPU with no warning. That includes the default-on case.
- State the supported subset explicitly and fail or warn when the config falls outside it.

findings.title: Core package takes server types, reversing the dependency direction
findings.description:
- `GpuAgentState.setup_from_server()` moves into the library package `migratory.gpu` (:294), but takes `EntityManager` and `WorldBoundsConfig`. These are `migratory_server` types, so the library would depend on the server.
- The move was justified as removing a production→bench dependency (:383), yet this adds a library→server one.
- Have the server-side driver unpack the primitives (arrays, `w`, `h`, `dt`, profiles) and pass them to a library initializer.

findings.title: Relocating `GpuAgentState` conflicts with "bench harness unchanged" and duplicates the tick sequence
findings.description:
- Out of scope says "any changes to the bench harness", and A5 says bench tests pass "without modification". The module move and import update (:294-296) is a change.
- The doc lists only `quadrants_fused_backend.py` as updated. Other importers (`runner.py`, bench tests) are not accounted for, and no re-export shim is mentioned.
- `GpuSimulationDriver.step()` re-implements the sequence from `QuadrantsFusedTickRunner.tick_once()`. The doc says "three phases" and then lists four (:119-123). That duplicates logic across bench and production and invites drift.
- Extract the tick sequence into `migratory.gpu` and have both callers use it. Alternatively, state explicitly why duplication is accepted.

findings.title: Precision contract differs from the parent plan, and the dependency list is incomplete
findings.description:
- The parent plan says slice 145's integrated tick uses f64 throughout on CUDA. This slice documents f32 GPU fields with an accepted deviation of about 1.37e-6.
- The slice also depends on `subdivision_factor` from slice 149 (:386) and on slice 147's gating. Frontmatter lists only 145, matching the plan entry.
- Reconcile the f32/f64 statement and add 149 to the dependencies.
- The Open Notes transfer estimate of ~200 KB at N=50k also looks understated: 50k × 2 components × 2 arrays is ~400 KB in f32 and ~800 KB in f64.

findings.title: Tier 2 NFR restated with a specific target
findings.description:
- A6 and the integration test restate the 60 TPS at N=50k gate.
- The slice keeps wire work out of scope, consistent with the plan's separation of compute and wire tracks.
- The config surface, startup validation, and one-way `server.py` → driver wiring are proportionate.
